study type: Retrospective population-based cohort study using registry data
exposure: Introduction of Doppler ultrasound in obstetric care
cohort: The study participants included approximately 1.2 million deliveries from the Medical Birth Registry of Norway between 1990 and 2014.
finding: The introduction of Doppler ultrasound contributed to a ~30% reduction in pre-term fetal deaths but had no effect on fetal death for term deliveries.
mod_finding: The introduction of Doppler ultrasound increased planned Caesarean sections by ~15% for pre-term deliveries, potentially contributing to the reduction in pre-term fetal deaths.
